title: The integers of a finite local-field extension are the integral closure
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $E\subseteq F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Give them their compatible extending $\ell$-adic absolute values, and put $\mathcal O_E=\{a\in E:|a|_E\leq1\}$ and $\mathcal O_F=\{x\in F:|x|_F\leq1\}$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Then, for every $x\in F$, $x\in\mathcal O_F$ if and only if $x$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\mathcal O_E$. Equivalently, $\mathcal O_F$ is the integral closure of $\mathcal O_E$ in $F$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: First sentence, the arithmetic input on O_F/O_E: valuation/integral-closure bridge implicit in the finite-module assertion. A textbook treatment is Serre, Local Fields, Ch. II, section 2, Proposition 3 and its corollaries (wanted, not obtained).

proof.text: Use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] to obtain the unit-ball membership descriptions for O_E and O_F, and the fraction-field and principal-ideal-ring structures on O_F. The coefficient absolute values are spectral norms by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. For the given injective Q_l-algebra homomorphism i, minpoly.algHom_eq identifies the minimal polynomials of a and i(a), so their spectral norms agree.

For x in O_F, its monic minimal polynomial over Q_l has spectral value at most one, by the definition of spectralNorm. Apply [lem-sfb-monic-spectral-value-coefficients] to bound every coefficient by one. Map this polynomial to E[T]. spectralNorm_extends shows that all mapped coefficients belong to O_E. Lift the mapped polynomial through O_E.subtype to a monic polynomial q over O_E, using Polynomial.lifts_iff_coeff_lifts and Polynomial.lifts_and_degree_eq_and_monic. The equation q.map O_E.subtype = (minpoly Q_l x).map (algebraMap Q_l E), the algebra-homomorphism identity i.commutes, and minpoly.aeval show that q evaluates to zero at x in F. Thus x is integral over O_E as in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

The principal ideal domain O_F is integrally closed by the normality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], and F is its fraction field. Compatibility of spectral norms proved in step 1 maps O_E into O_F. Subring.integralClosure_le_iff therefore puts the integral closure of O_E in F inside O_F: an element integral over O_E is also integral over O_F, hence belongs to O_F. Together with step 2 this proves the equivalence unchanged.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q59-7d9f08ded (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement is unchanged, and it is exactly what step 1 of the parent det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free uses: O_F is the integral closure of O_E, taken before the finite-closure theorem (032L). The delivery creates no new nodes, so no drop is needed. Steps checked against the cited statements: (1) Q_l is complete and its norm is nontrivial (|l|=1/l<1). With base Q_l, V=F and W=Q_l^d, every hypothesis of lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism holds, so the coordinate maps are continuous. (2) The ε-box argument shows that every power x^n, including n=0, lies in L=sum Z_l l^{-N} b_i. (3) A DVR is a PID, hence Noetherian (lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal). Z_l[x] is a submodule of L, so it is finite by lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite; the step does not claim L is a ring. (4) finite-algebra-is-integral applies to Z_l[x]. Since Z_l is contained in O_E, the same monic equation makes x integral over O_E. (5) The ultrametric estimate t^r<=t^{r-1}<t^r for t=|x|>1 is a genuinely elementary step. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Small cases pass: x=0, units, E=F=Q_l, l=2, r=1, and the totally ramified Q_l(l^{1/e}). There is no cycle: the closure of the 9 dependencies (28 nodes) does not reach the item, and its only citer is the parent. Off-unit citations are only Mathlib leaves and a definition, so no tool_uses is needed; removing the self-written request was correct (C8). Duplicate check over dag/nodes and the main-20261015 blueprint: the DVR, localization and Gauss-lemma nodes and the normalization nodes are not duplicates, so same_as=[] is right. Mathlib: Valuation.Integers.isIntegral_iff_v_le_one (Integral.lean:35) assumes O is the whole unit ball in the same ring, so it is not a leaf; the searches cover all three required kinds. Serre is honestly recorded as WANTED, with proof_origin=agent. No SGA is used and this is not a target node. No fixes were written.
